# `ingress.interval_s` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the HTTP ingress gateway that accepts messages over REST.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `300` |
| Available since | 2.1 |
| Component | ingress |
| Unit | s |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `ingress.interval_s` only if you observe problems with the HTTP ingress gateway that accepts messages over REST, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[ingress]
interval_s = 300
```

# `pq snapshot describe`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Describes a snapshot.

## Usage
```
pq snapshot describe <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--since` | Only consider objects created after this timestamp (ISO 8601). |
| `--wait` | Block until the operation is completed on all nodes. |
| `--include-internal` | Also show internal system objects (names starting with `__`). |
| `--tenant` | Name of the tenant the command applies to. |

## Example
```
pq snapshot describe orders --since
```

# Runbook: snapshotter troubleshooting

> Operations runbook

This runbook covers the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

## Health check
1. Run `pq node describe <node> --output json` and check the `snapshotter` section.
2. Look at the `paderqueue_snapshotter_errors_total` metric.

## Relevant settings
- `snapshotter.batch_size`
- `snapshotter.buffer_bytes`
- `snapshotter.max_retries`
- `snapshotter.max_connections`
- `snapshotter.queue_capacity`
- `snapshotter.enabled`
- `snapshotter.threshold_percent`
- `snapshotter.log_level`

## Escalation
If the problem persists for more than 30 minutes, escalate to the platform team.

# PaderQueue 2.0 release notes

Released on 2022-04-11.

This is a major release. Read the section on changed defaults before upgrading.

## New features

- New option `compactor.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `partitioner.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E2051 (COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New option `spool.compression`: compression codec that the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments uses for stored or transferred data.

- New error code PQ-E3575 (COORDINATOR_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4426 (SCHEDULER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4708 (SCHEDULER_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.compression`: compression codec that the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers uses for stored or transferred data.

- New option `dlq.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

Type: error

# PQ-E3239 QUOTA_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `quota: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
A request needed the quota, but the quota is switched off.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `quota.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

- New option `coordinator.enabled`: turns the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers on or off.

- New option `compactor.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `dlq.enabled`: turns the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue on or off.

- New option `compactor.batch_size`: number of messages the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages processes together in one batch.

Title: retention.batch_size
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `retention.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `256` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | retention |
| Unit | messages |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `retention.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[retention]
batch_size = 256
```

# PQ-E4708 SCHEDULER_THROTTLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: throttled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The scheduler is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `scheduler.threshold_percent`.

# PQ-E3239 QUOTA_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `quota: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
A request needed the quota, but the quota is switched off.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `quota.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

# PQ-E2051 COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the compactor use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `compactor.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# PaderQueue 1.1 release notes

Released on 2021-07-19.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.batch_size`: number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

- New option `metrics.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `snapshotter.enabled`: turns the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues on or off.

- New option `auth.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the authentication module that validates client tokens waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `dlq.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `partitioner.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1616 (PARTITIONER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# PQ-E4712 SNAPSHOTTER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: work queue full`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 1.2

## What it means
The internal work queue of the snapshotter is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `snapshotter.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E3441 ACKTRACKER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the acktracker is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `acktracker.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

# PQ-E2400 SPOOL_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `spool: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 3.2

## What it means
The spool gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `spool.max_retries`.

# PQ-E2602 COORDINATOR_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `coordinator: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The internal work queue of the coordinator is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `coordinator.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# Postmortem INC-2025-114: inventory-sync degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 55 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `inventory-sync`

## Summary
During the incident, `inventory-sync` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2602 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `inventory-sync` fired.
- T+13: On-call engineer found PQ-E2602 in the broker logs.
- T+27: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+55: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2602.
- Add an alert for this error code.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `coordinator: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The internal work queue of the coordinator is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `coordinator.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# PaderQueue 2.0 release notes

Released on 2022-04-11.

This is a major release. Read the section on changed defaults before upgrading.

## New features

- New option `compactor.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `partitioner.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E2051 (COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New option `spool.compression`: compression codec that the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments uses for stored or transferred data.

- New error code PQ-E3575 (COORDINATOR_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4426 (SCHEDULER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4708 (SCHEDULER_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.compression`: compression codec that the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers uses for stored or transferred data.

- New option `dlq.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

# Postmortem INC-2024-160: search-indexer degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 140 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `search-indexer`

## Summary
During the incident, `search-indexer` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2771 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `search-indexer` fired.
- T+35: On-call engineer found PQ-E2771 in the broker logs.
- T+70: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+140: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2771.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `snapshotter.max_retries` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Maximum number of retry attempts of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues before an operation is reported as failed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `8` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | snapshotter |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `snapshotter.max_retries` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[snapshotter]
max_retries = 8
```

Title: spool.batch_size
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `spool.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `100` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | spool |
| Unit | messages |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `spool.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[spool]
batch_size = 100
```

Title: Runbook: spool troubleshooting
Type: runbook
Version: 4.x

# Runbook: spool troubleshooting

> Operations runbook

This runbook covers the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

## Health check
1. Run `pq node describe <node> --output json` and check the `spool` section.
2. Look at the `paderqueue_spool_errors_total` metric.

## Relevant settings
- `spool.max_connections`
- `spool.max_retries`
- `spool.enabled`
- `spool.compression`
- `spool.threshold_percent`
- `spool.batch_size`
- `spool.log_level`
- `spool.interval_s`

## Escalation
If the problem persists for more than 30 minutes, escalate to the platform team.

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `33554432` |
| Available since | 3.0 |
| Component | broker |
| Unit | bytes |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `broker.buffer_bytes` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[broker]
buffer_bytes = 33554432
```

# `coordinator.buffer_bytes` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `4194304` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | bytes |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `coordinator.buffer_bytes` only if you observe problems with the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[coordinator]
buffer_bytes = 4194304
```

# PQ-E3221 BROKER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the broker is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `broker.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

Title: Postmortem INC-2025-175
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2025-175: chat-relay degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 90 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `chat-relay`

## Summary
During the incident, `chat-relay` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2617 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `chat-relay` fired.
- T+22: On-call engineer found PQ-E2617 in the broker logs.
- T+45: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+90: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2617.
- Add an alert for this error code.

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `fraud-scoring`

## Summary
During the incident, `fraud-scoring` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2051 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `fraud-scoring` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E2051 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2051.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: PaderQueue 3.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 3.1

# PaderQueue 3.1 release notes

Released on 2024-01-15.

## New features

- New option `acktracker.batch_size`: number of messages the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E1176 (INGRESS_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `spool.log_level`: log verbosity of the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `compactor.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `broker.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.enabled`: turns the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers on or off.

- New option `compactor.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `dlq.enabled`: turns the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue on or off.

- New option `compactor.batch_size`: number of messages the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages processes together in one batch.

Title: dlq.timeout_ms
Type: config

# `dlq.timeout_ms`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `10000` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | dlq |
| Unit | ms |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `dlq.timeout_ms` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[dlq]
timeout_ms = 10000
```

Type: config
Version: 3.x

# `dlq.timeout_ms` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `30000` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | dlq |
| Unit | ms |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `dlq.timeout_ms` only if you observe problems with the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[dlq]
timeout_ms = 30000
```

Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2771 DLQ_OPERATION_TIMEOUT

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `dlq: operation timeout`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
An operation of the dlq did not complete within the configured timeout.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Check network latency and load on the involved nodes. For slow but healthy clusters, increase `dlq.timeout_ms`.

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

# PaderQueue 1.1 release notes

Released on 2021-07-19.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.batch_size`: number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

- New option `metrics.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `snapshotter.enabled`: turns the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues on or off.

- New option `auth.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the authentication module that validates client tokens waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `dlq.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `partitioner.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1616 (PARTITIONER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# `partitioner.buffer_bytes` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `1048576` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |

## Notes

Changes to `partitioner.buffer_bytes` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 1048576
```

Document: d0738
Title: PQ-E2051 COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2051 COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the compactor use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `compactor.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

Document: d0048
Title: Postmortem INC-2024-185
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-185: fraud-scoring degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `fraud-scoring`

## Summary
During the incident, `fraud-scoring` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2051 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `fraud-scoring` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E2051 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2051.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E3221 BROKER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the broker is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `broker.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-211
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-211: search-indexer degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 25 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `search-indexer`

## Summary
During the incident, `search-indexer` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3221 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `search-indexer` fired.
- T+6: On-call engineer found PQ-E3221 in the broker logs.
- T+12: The team rolled back the last client deployment.
- T+25: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a failing disk on one node.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3221.
- Add an alert for this error code.

- New error code PQ-E2470 (SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `retention.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `replicator.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E2622 (QUOTA_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New option `metrics.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New error code PQ-E3221 (BROKER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `broker.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E4582 (RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED) with a clearer log message.

# PaderQueue 3.1 release notes

Released on 2024-01-15.

## New features

- New option `acktracker.batch_size`: number of messages the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E1176 (INGRESS_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `spool.log_level`: log verbosity of the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `compactor.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `broker.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.enabled`: turns the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers on or off.

# PQ-E4895 REPLICATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `replicator: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the replicator use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Set `replicator.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# Postmortem INC-2025-174: user-activity degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 40 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `user-activity`

## Summary
During the incident, `user-activity` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4798 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `user-activity` fired.
- T+10: On-call engineer found PQ-E4798 in the broker logs.
- T+20: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+40: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4798.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PaderQueue 3.1 release notes

Released on 2024-01-15.

## New features

- New option `acktracker.batch_size`: number of messages the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E1176 (INGRESS_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `spool.log_level`: log verbosity of the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `compactor.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `broker.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.enabled`: turns the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers on or off.

- New option `compactor.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `dlq.enabled`: turns the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue on or off.

- New option `compactor.batch_size`: number of messages the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages processes together in one batch.

# `scheduler.max_retries`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of retry attempts of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time before an operation is reported as failed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `5` |
| Available since | 3.0 |
| Component | scheduler |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `scheduler.max_retries` only if you observe problems with the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[scheduler]
max_retries = 5
```

# PQ-E1441 COORDINATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `coordinator: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the coordinator use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `coordinator.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

[compactor]

# PQ-E4582 RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `retention: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The retention refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `retention.max_connections`.

# Postmortem INC-2025-126: chat-relay degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 210 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `chat-relay`

## Summary
During the incident, `chat-relay` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4895 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `chat-relay` fired.
- T+52: On-call engineer found PQ-E4895 in the broker logs.
- T+105: The team restarted the affected nodes.
- T+210: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4895.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `dlq.batch_size` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Number of messages the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `100` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | dlq |
| Unit | messages |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `dlq.batch_size` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[dlq]
batch_size = 100
```

Document: d0122
Title: acktracker.enabled
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `acktracker.enabled`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Turns the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed on or off.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `true` |
| Available since | 3.1 |
| Component | acktracker |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `acktracker.enabled` only if you observe problems with the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[acktracker]
enabled = true
```

- T+90: Service recovered.

Title: PQ-E1163 SNAPSHOTTER_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E1163 SNAPSHOTTER_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The snapshotter refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `snapshotter.max_connections`.

Type: config

# `quota.max_retries`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of retry attempts of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant before an operation is reported as failed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `8` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | quota |

## Notes

Changes to `quota.max_retries` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[quota]
max_retries = 8
```

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `billing-events`

## Summary
During the incident, `billing-events` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3177 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `billing-events` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E3177 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3177.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E4712 SNAPSHOTTER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: work queue full`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 1.2

## What it means
The internal work queue of the snapshotter is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `snapshotter.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

The retention refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

Title: acktracker.interval_s
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `acktracker.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `30` |
| Available since | 3.0 |
| Component | acktracker |
| Unit | s |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `acktracker.interval_s` only if you observe problems with the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[acktracker]
interval_s = 30
```

Type: runbook
Version: 4.x

# Runbook: acktracker troubleshooting

> Operations runbook

This runbook covers the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

## Health check
1. Run `pq node describe <node> --output json` and check the `acktracker` section.
2. Look at the `paderqueue_acktracker_errors_total` metric.

## Relevant settings
- `acktracker.timeout_ms`
- `acktracker.max_retries`
- `acktracker.buffer_bytes`
- `acktracker.max_connections`
- `acktracker.batch_size`
- `acktracker.interval_s`
- `acktracker.enabled`
- `acktracker.queue_capacity`

## Escalation
If the problem persists for more than 30 minutes, escalate to the platform team.

Title: PQ-E4007 BROKER_CODEC_MISMATCH
Type: error

# PQ-E4007 BROKER_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the broker use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Set `broker.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

Document: d0406
Title: PaderQueue 3.0 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 3.0

(previously `300`). - **Changed default:** `snapshotter.max_connections` now defaults to `512` (previously `256`). - **Changed default:** `metrics.interval_s` now defaults to `10` (previously `300`). - **Changed default:** `scheduler.log_level` now defaults to `info` (previously `error`).

## New features

- New option `retention.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period.

- New option `ingress.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the HTTP ingress gateway that accepts messages over REST starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1441 (COORDINATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4572 (QUOTA_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `broker.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues, in bytes.

- New option `metrics.log_level`: log verbosity of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `acktracker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New option `quota.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant.

- New error code PQ-E4007 (BROKER_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2154 (QUOTA_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E3891 (COMPACTOR_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New error code PQ-E2758 (RETENTION_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

# PQ-E3177 SCHEDULER_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.2

## What it means
The scheduler refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `scheduler.max_connections`.

showed error PQ-E3177 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `billing-events` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E3177 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3177.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `dlq.timeout_ms` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `30000` |
| Available since | 1.1 |

The default works for most deployments. Change `dlq.timeout_ms` only if you observe problems with the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[dlq]
timeout_ms = 30000
```

# Runbook: coordinator troubleshooting

> Operations runbook

This runbook covers the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

## Health check
1. Run `pq node describe <node> --output json` and check the `coordinator` section.
2. Look at the `paderqueue_coordinator_errors_total` metric.

## Relevant settings
- `coordinator.batch_size`
- `coordinator.worker_threads`
- `coordinator.max_connections`
- `coordinator.buffer_bytes`
- `coordinator.queue_capacity`
- `coordinator.threshold_percent`
- `coordinator.enabled`
- `coordinator.compression`

## Escalation
If the problem persists for more than 30 minutes, escalate to the platform team.

# `pq tenant export`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Exports a tenant.

```
pq tenant export <name> [flags]

|---|---|

| `--label` | Attach a `key=value` label. Can be repeated. |
| `--retain-days` | Number of days the result is kept before it is deleted automatically. |

pq tenant export orders --timeout
```

# PQ-E2470 SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
A request needed the snapshotter, but the snapshotter is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `snapshotter.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `dlq: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the dlq use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Set `dlq.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

Maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

|---|---|

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `partitioner.max_retries` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
max_retries = 3
```

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

# PaderQueue 1.1 release notes

Released on 2021-07-19.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.batch_size`: number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

- New option `metrics.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `snapshotter.enabled`: turns the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues on or off.

- New option `auth.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the authentication module that validates client tokens waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `dlq.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `partitioner.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1616 (PARTITIONER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

[dlq]

```

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-147
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-147: search-indexer degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 40 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `search-indexer`

## Summary
During the incident, `search-indexer` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2051 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `search-indexer` fired.
- T+10: On-call engineer found PQ-E2051 in the broker logs.
- T+20: The team rolled back the last client deployment.
- T+40: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a failing disk on one node.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2051.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: PaderQueue 3.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 3.1

# PaderQueue 3.1 release notes

Released on 2024-01-15.

## New features

- New option `acktracker.batch_size`: number of messages the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E1176 (INGRESS_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `spool.log_level`: log verbosity of the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `compactor.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `broker.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.enabled`: turns the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers on or off.

- New option `compactor.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `dlq.enabled`: turns the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue on or off.

- New option `compactor.batch_size`: number of messages the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages processes together in one batch.

Type: error

# PQ-E4007 BROKER_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the broker use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Set `broker.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

Title: partitioner.batch_size
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `partitioner.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `256` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | messages |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
batch_size = 256
```

# `pq queue describe`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Describes a queue.

## Usage
```
pq queue describe <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--include-internal` | Also show internal system objects (names starting with `__`). |
| `--retain-days` | Number of days the result is kept before it is deleted automatically. |
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for the operation to finish. Default: 30. |

## Example
```
pq queue describe orders --include-internal
```

# `pq snapshot describe`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Describes a snapshot.

## Usage
```
pq snapshot describe <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--since` | Only consider objects created after this timestamp (ISO 8601). |
| `--wait` | Block until the operation is completed on all nodes. |
| `--include-internal` | Also show internal system objects (names starting with `__`). |
| `--tenant` | Name of the tenant the command applies to. |

## Example
```
pq snapshot describe orders --since
```

Title: PaderQueue 1.2 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.2

in the internal work queue of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant. - New option `quota.enabled`: turns the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant on or off.

- New option `spool.batch_size`: number of messages the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments processes together in one batch.

- New option `partitioner.compression`: compression codec that the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written uses for stored or transferred data.

- New option `snapshotter.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E4712 (SNAPSHOTTER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `retention.log_level`: log verbosity of the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period.

- New option `coordinator.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, in bytes.

- New option `partitioner.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written.

- New option `quota.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant before an operation is reported as failed.

- New option `coordinator.batch_size`: number of messages the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers processes together in one batch.

- New option `replicator.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `snapshotter.queue_capacity` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

[snapshotter]

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-166

# Postmortem INC-2024-166: fraud-scoring degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 40 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `fraud-scoring`

## Summary
During the incident, `fraud-scoring` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4013 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `fraud-scoring` fired.
- T+10: On-call engineer found PQ-E4013 in the broker logs.
- T+20: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+40: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4013.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E1465 INGRESS_OPERATION_TIMEOUT

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `ingress: operation timeout`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
An operation of the ingress did not complete within the configured timeout.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Check network latency and load on the involved nodes. For slow but healthy clusters, increase `ingress.timeout_ms`.

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-135
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-135: chat-relay degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 40 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `chat-relay`

## Summary
During the incident, `chat-relay` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3575 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `chat-relay` fired.
- T+10: On-call engineer found PQ-E3575 in the broker logs.
- T+20: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+40: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3575.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Type: error

# PQ-E2470 SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
A request needed the snapshotter, but the snapshotter is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `snapshotter.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: throttled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The scheduler is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `scheduler.threshold_percent`.

Title: PaderQueue 3.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 3.1

undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue on or off. - New option `compactor.batch_size`: number of messages the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E3249 (ACKTRACKER_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.enabled`: turns the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed on or off.

- New error code PQ-E3841 (REPLICATOR_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E1405 (BROKER_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `scheduler.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `metrics.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics starts throttling.

## Bug fixes and improvements

- Fixed a race condition in the partitioner during node shutdown.
- Fixed a crash of the ingress when the configuration file contained trailing whitespace.
- The compactor now logs its effective configuration at startup.
- Fixed a race condition in the scheduler during node shutdown.
- The snapshotter now logs its effective configuration at startup.
- Improved startup time of the scheduler.

# Postmortem INC-2024-136: report-builder degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `report-builder`

## Summary
During the incident, `report-builder` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2758 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `report-builder` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E2758 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team restarted the affected nodes.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2758.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `partitioner.compression`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Compression codec that the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written uses for stored or transferred data.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | enum: none | lz4 | zstd |
| Default | `none` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.compression` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
compression = "none"
```

Title: PQ-E2451 SNAPSHOTTER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2451 SNAPSHOTTER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 3.2

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the snapshotter is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `snapshotter.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

# PQ-E3642 ACKTRACKER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the acktracker is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `acktracker.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

The ingress is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

- Too many tenants on one node

Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `ingress.threshold_percent`.

# PaderQueue 2.2 release notes

Released on 2022-12-12.

## New features

- New option `broker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `acktracker.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New error code PQ-E4371 (ACKTRACKER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4711 (ACKTRACKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New option `snapshotter.log_level`: log verbosity of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E3828 (METRICS_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E3239 (QUOTA_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `dlq.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

- New option `metrics.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics before an operation is reported as failed.

Document: d0805
Title: PaderQueue 2.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 2.1

releases delayed messages at their due time. - New option `spool.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `replicator.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `acktracker.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1799 (RETENTION_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2425 (ACKTRACKER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `broker.enabled`: turns the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues on or off.

- New option `broker.batch_size`: number of messages the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues processes together in one batch.

- New option `spool.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments starts throttling.

- New option `spool.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

- New option `coordinator.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New error code PQ-E1779 (INGRESS_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E1465 (INGRESS_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E3114 (SPOOL_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# `pq snapshot create`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Creates a snapshot.

## Usage
```
pq snapshot create <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for the operation to finish. Default: 30. |
| `--max-parallel` | Maximum number of nodes processed at the same time. Default: 2. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without changing anything. |
| `--force` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |

## Example
```
pq snapshot create orders --timeout
```

# PaderQueue 2.0 release notes

Released on 2022-04-11.

This is a major release. Read the section on changed defaults before upgrading.

## New features

- New option `compactor.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

- New option `partitioner.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E2051 (COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New option `spool.compression`: compression codec that the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments uses for stored or transferred data.

- New error code PQ-E3575 (COORDINATOR_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4426 (SCHEDULER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4708 (SCHEDULER_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.compression`: compression codec that the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers uses for stored or transferred data.

- New option `dlq.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

Type: config

# `acktracker.max_connections`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `128` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | acktracker |
| Unit | connections |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `acktracker.max_connections` only if you observe problems with the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[acktracker]
max_connections = 128
```

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `acktracker.buffer_bytes` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

# PQ-E4582 RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `retention: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The retention refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `retention.max_connections`.

# Postmortem INC-2024-214: inventory-sync degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 210 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `inventory-sync`

## Summary
During the incident, `inventory-sync` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3792 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `inventory-sync` fired.
- T+52: On-call engineer found PQ-E3792 in the broker logs.
- T+105: The team rolled back the last client deployment.
- T+210: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3792.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `partitioner.buffer_bytes` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `1048576` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |

## Notes

Changes to `partitioner.buffer_bytes` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 1048576
```

Title: pq schedule create
Type: cli
Version: 4.x

# `pq schedule create`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Creates a schedule.

## Usage
```
pq schedule create <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--tenant` | Name of the tenant the command applies to. |
| `--output` | Output format: `table`, `json` or `yaml`. Default: `table`. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without changing anything. |
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for the operation to finish. Default: 30. |

## Example
```
pq schedule create orders --tenant
```

Title: pq snapshot create
Type: cli
Version: 4.x

# `pq snapshot create`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Creates a snapshot.

## Usage
```
pq snapshot create <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for the operation to finish. Default: 30. |
| `--max-parallel` | Maximum number of nodes processed at the same time. Default: 2. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without changing anything. |
| `--force` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |

## Example
```
pq snapshot create orders --timeout
```

Title: replicator.max_connections (PaderQueue 3.x)
Type: config
Version: 3.x

# `replicator.max_connections` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `1024` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | replicator |
| Unit | connections |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `replicator.max_connections` only if you observe problems with the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[replicator]
max_connections = 1024
```

Title: replicator.max_connections
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `replicator.max_connections`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `4096` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | replicator |
| Unit | connections |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## Notes

Changes to `replicator.max_connections` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[replicator]
max_connections = 4096
```

Title: PQ-E4964 DLQ_CODEC_MISMATCH
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E4964 DLQ_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `dlq: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the dlq use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Set `dlq.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.0

A request needed the snapshotter, but the snapshotter is switched off.

Enable the component by setting `snapshotter.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

# PQ-E4708 SCHEDULER_THROTTLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: throttled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The scheduler is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `scheduler.threshold_percent`.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[scheduler]
threshold_percent = 75
```

Title: Runbook: scheduler troubleshooting
Type: runbook
Version: 4.x

# Runbook: scheduler troubleshooting

> Operations runbook

This runbook covers the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

## Health check
1. Run `pq node describe <node> --output json` and check the `scheduler` section.
2. Look at the `paderqueue_scheduler_errors_total` metric.

## Relevant settings
- `scheduler.log_level`
- `scheduler.buffer_bytes`
- `scheduler.queue_capacity`
- `scheduler.threshold_percent`
- `scheduler.batch_size`
- `scheduler.max_connections`
- `scheduler.interval_s`
- `scheduler.max_retries`

## Escalation
If the problem persists for more than 30 minutes, escalate to the platform team.

Title: replicator.worker_threads
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `replicator.worker_threads`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `1` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | replicator |
| Unit | threads |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `replicator.worker_threads` only if you observe problems with the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[replicator]
worker_threads = 1
```

# PQ-E4582 RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `retention: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The retention refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `retention.max_connections`.

Title: PaderQueue 1.0 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.0

# PaderQueue 1.0 release notes

Released on 2021-03-02.

## New features

- New error code PQ-E2470 (SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `retention.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `replicator.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes, in bytes.

- New option `metrics.batch_size`: number of messages the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics processes together in one batch.

- New error code PQ-E4934 (SPOOL_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4964 (DLQ_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E2622 (QUOTA_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New option `metrics.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New error code PQ-E3221 (BROKER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `broker.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E4582 (RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED) with a clearer log message.

# PQ-E4582 RETENTION_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `retention: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
The retention refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `retention.max_connections`.

# Postmortem INC-2024-178: billing-events degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 210 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `billing-events`

## Summary
During the incident, `billing-events` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4582 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `billing-events` fired.
- T+52: On-call engineer found PQ-E4582 in the broker logs.
- T+105: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+210: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4582.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the compactor that merges old log segments and removes superseded messages.

|---|---|

```toml
[compactor]

```

- `compactor.enabled`

- `compactor.worker_threads`

- `compactor.compression`

Title: PQ-E2470 SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2470 SNAPSHOTTER_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
A request needed the snapshotter, but the snapshotter is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `snapshotter.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: throttled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The scheduler is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `scheduler.threshold_percent`.

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `4194304` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | bytes |

The default works for most deployments. Change `coordinator.buffer_bytes` only if you observe problems with the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[coordinator]
buffer_bytes = 4194304
```
